summary: Betts and Stix prove that for a number field K with no CM subfield and a curve Y/K of genus ≥ 2, the image of the Selmer sections in Y(K_v) is finite for every finite place v (Theorem A), and hence that each local projection of the finite descent locus is finite (Theorem B). The method recasts Lawrence–Venkatesh as an obstruction. A Selmer section restricts the cohomology local systems of an abelian-by-finite family to a global symplectic pair interpolating the local ones (Theorem 7.1). For every self-conjugate v, a Kodaira–Parshin family has finite Lawrence–Venkatesh locus (Theorem 6.5); this rests on model-free v-adic period maps, which control D_pst via Scholze's relative comparison and Shimizu's horizontal semistability, and on a symplectic principal trichotomy. As the maintainer routed it, the new mathematics goes to a Part II of the anabelian roadmap (GaloisSectionsPadicPeriodMaps); Lawrence–Venkatesh machinery is sourced into LV.1, LV.2, LV.3 and LV.7, relative p-adic Hodge theory into PadicHodgeTheory P8, and the Chern-class compatibility into CohomologyComparisons CP.6. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, and every missing item is routed exactly once. Six findings are recorded, including a counterexample to Proposition 6.7(c) as printed for non-reduced A (not used), and two proof gaps with easy repairs. The published revision was not available for comparison. Not formalised.

items.name: Galois sections of a curve
items.statement: For a smooth projective geometrically connected curve Y/K of genus ≥ 2 over a number field, Sec(Y/K) is the set of π_1^ét(Y_K̄)-conjugacy classes of splittings of 1 → π_1^ét(Y_K̄) → π_1^ét(Y) → G_K → 1 (1.1); each y ∈ Y(K) gives one, and the Section Conjecture predicts that these are all, each arising from a unique y.

items.name: Selmer sections and the localisation maps
items.statement: A section s is Selmer when, for every place u of K, its restriction s|G_u to a decomposition group is the section of a K_u-rational point y_u ∈ Y(K_u). Sec^Sel(Y/K) is the set of Selmer sections, and for finite u, loc_u: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(K_u) sends s to the unique y_u giving s|G_u.

items.name: Theorem A
items.statement: Let K be a number field containing no CM subfield and Y/K a smooth projective curve of genus ≥ 2. Then for every finite place v of K the image of loc_v: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(K_v) is finite.
items.note: Proof: Theorem 7.1 and Lemma 6.4 put the image in Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S}; Theorem 6.5 makes that finite for the Kodaira–Parshin family; with no CM subfield every place is self-conjugate (Remark 2.18(1)).

items.name: Modified adelic points and the finite descent locus
items.statement: Y(A_K)_• is the product of Y(K_v) over finite v with π_0(Y(K_v)) over archimedean v [Sto07, §2]; the finite descent locus Y(A_K)_•^{f-cov} ⊆ Y(A_K)_• contains Y(K) and is conjecturally equal to it [Sto07, Conjecture 9.1].
items.note: RP.3 plans descent sets and their comparison with finite étale descent.

items.name: Harari–Stix: finite descent and Selmer sections (cited)
items.statement: Y(A_K)_•^{f-cov} is exactly the image of Sec^Sel(Y/K) under the total localisation map loc: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(A_K)_• [HS12, Theorem 11].

items.name: Theorem B
items.statement: Let K be a number field containing no CM subfield and Y/K a smooth projective curve of genus ≥ 2. Then for every finite place v of K the projection of Y(A_K)_•^{f-cov} to Y(K_v) is finite.

items.name: The Lawrence–Venkatesh argument as an obstruction (Remark 1.3)
items.statement: [LV20] essentially proves (1°) Y(K) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} for every abelian-by-finite family, suitable S and finite v | p, and (2°) for some finite v | p and odd prime q, Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} is finite for all suitable S. With bookkeeping, Theorem A follows for 100% of places when K has no CM subfield (Remark 6.23(I)); the original method never covers places ramified over Q, places above 2, or places of bad reduction.
items.locator: arXiv v1 Remark 1.3 and footnote 1, p.3
items.note: Footnote 1: [LV20, §3.4] treats residue disks centred at K-points only; §5 extends it to K_v-points.

items.name: The non-symplectic locus (Remark 1.4)
items.statement: Y(K_v)^{LV°}_{X,S} is defined as in Definition 1.2 with 'symplectic' omitted throughout; Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} ⊆ Y(K_v)^{LV°}_{X,S}. For Y of genus 3 over Q the original argument needs the Kodaira–Parshin family with q ≥ 23 (relative dimension ≥ 55), whereas the symplectic formulation works with q = 11 (relative dimension 25).
items.note: Checked by cc-442dc5 against Remark 6.23(III): d_q = (g − 1/2)(q − 1) gives 55 and 25.

items.name: Local systems constrain Selmer sections (Remark 1.5)
items.statement: Any v-adic obstruction to K-rational points coming from a Q_p-local system on Y also constrains the image of loc_v: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(K_v), by restricting the corresponding π_1^ét(Y)-representation along the section.

items.name: Purity and integrality
items.statement: A q-Weil number of weight n is algebraic with |ι(α)| = q^{n/2} for all complex embeddings ι. An unramified representation of G_u (u ∤ p∞) is pure of weight n if the geometric Frobenius eigenvalues are q_u-Weil numbers of weight n, and integral if the characteristic polynomial of geometric Frobenius has coefficients in Z.

items.name: Example 2.2: étale cohomology is pure outside S
items.statement: For a smooth proper variety X over a number field K there is a finite set S of places, containing those above p∞, outside which H^n_ét(X_K̄, Q_p) is unramified, pure and integral of weight n (smooth proper base change and [Del74, Théorème 1.6]).

items.name: Symplectic representations and GSp-irreducibility
items.statement: A symplectic Galois representation is (V, L, ω) with L one-dimensional and ω: ∧²V → L a perfect Galois-equivariant alternating pairing (usually L = Q_p(−1)); it is GSp-irreducible if V has no non-zero G_K-stable isotropic subspace, i.e. the image does not lie in a proper parabolic subgroup of GSp.

items.name: Lemma 2.4: symplectic Faltings lemma (cited)
items.statement: Let S contain the places above p∞, n ≥ 0 and d > 0. Up to isomorphism there are only finitely many GSp-irreducible symplectic representations (V, L, ω) of G_K with V of rank 2d, unramified, pure and integral of weight n outside S [LV20, Lemma 2.6].
items.note: The Lawrence–Venkatesh roadmap's LV.1 plans Faltings's lemma in its semisimple form (LV Lemma 2.3); this paper uses the symplectic version, so it is a source for LV.1.

items.name: De Rham representations
items.statement: For a G_v-representation V, D_dR(V) := (B_dR ⊗_{Q_p} V)^{G_v} has K_v-dimension ≤ dim V, with equality defining de Rham representations; these form a full ⊗-subcategory Rep^dR(G_v) closed under subobjects, with a ⊗-functorial Hodge filtration F^• on D_dR(V).

items.name: Filtered discrete (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules
items.statement: A (ϕ, N, G_v)-module is a Q_p^nr-vector space with bijective semilinear Frobenius ϕ, linear monodromy N and a semilinear G_v-action, with Nϕ = pϕN and N, ϕ commuting with G_v; it is discrete if point stabilisers are open. A filtered discrete one is (D_pst, D_dR, c_BO) with D_dR a filtered K_v-vector space and c_BO: K̄_v ⊗ D_pst ≅ K̄_v ⊗ D_dR a G_v-equivariant isomorphism; they form the ⊗-category MF(ϕ, N, G_v).
items.note: R06.2 plans filtered (φ, N)-modules with descent data.

items.name: D_pst and D_pH
items.statement: D_pst(V) := lim_w (B_st ⊗ V)^{G_w} (colimit over open G_w ≤ G_v) is a discrete (ϕ, N, G_v)-module of dimension ≤ dim V, with equality for de Rham V [Ber02, Théorème 0.7]; then c_BO is an isomorphism and D_pH(V) := (D_pst(V), D_dR(V), c_BO). B_st is identified with its image in B_dR independently of a choice of p-adic logarithm, as in [Shi20]. Example 2.8: a proper smooth O_v-scheme gives one through crystalline cohomology and Berthelot–Ogus.

items.name: Theorem 2.9 (Fontaine, Berger)
items.statement: V ↦ D_pH(V) is a fully faithful ⊗-functor Rep^dR_{Q_p}(G_v) ↪ MF(ϕ, N, G_v) [Fon94b, Théorème 5.6.7(v)], [Ber02, Théorème 0.7].

items.name: p-adic Hodge cohomology
items.statement: For a variety X over a finite extension L_w of K_v, H^•_pH(X/L_w) := (H^•_pst(X/Q_p^nr), H^•_dR(X/L_w), c_dR ∘ c_BO) with H^•_pst := D_pst(H^•_ét(X_{L̄_w}, Q_p)) and c_dR Scholze's comparison isomorphism (3.8); it is contravariantly functorial in X (Proposition 3.19(2)).
items.note: Remark 2.11: functoriality is proved for this particular c_dR, not quoted from [Tsu02].

items.name: Restriction and induction of filtered (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules
items.statement: For L_w/K_v finite in K̄_v: restriction D ↦ D|G_w := (D_pst|G_w, L_w ⊗ D_dR, c_BO), a ⊗-functor, and induction Ind_{G_w}^{G_v} D := (Ind D_pst, D_dR as a K_v-space, c'_BO), a lax ⊗-functor right adjoint to restriction. Example 2.12: H^•_pH(X_{L_w}/L_w) ≅ H^•_pH(X/K_v)|G_w (2.1) and, for X over L_w, H^•_pH(X/K_v) ≅ Ind H^•_pH(X/L_w) (2.2).

items.name: Automorphism groups of (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules and the modules M(Φ)
items.statement: Aut(D) is the functor R ↦ R-linear automorphisms of R ⊗ D commuting with ϕ, N and G_v; for a symplectic (ϕ, N, G_v)-module, Aut^GSp(D) ⊆ Aut(D) preserves ω up to a similitude factor; scalars give a central G_m. Aut(D_pst) acts on Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} of the flag variety G of filtrations on D_dR (Remark 2.14), and M(Φ) := (D_pst, D_dR, c_BO) with the filtration Φ in place of the given one.

items.name: Lemma 2.15: the orbit lemma
items.statement: M(Φ_1) ≅ M(Φ_2) as filtered discrete (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules if and only if Φ_1, Φ_2 lie in one Aut(D_pst)(Q_p)-orbit; so the Φ with M(Φ) in a fixed isomorphism class lie in a Q_p-subvariety of Res^{K_v}_{Q_p} G of dimension ≤ dim_{Q_p} Aut(D_pst).
items.note: Generalises the Lawrence–Venkatesh orbit lemma (LV.4) from filtered φ-modules.

items.name: Proposition 2.16: dimension bounds
items.statement: (1) For a (ϕ, N, G_v)-module D of Q_p^nr-dimension d, Aut(D) is a Q_p-algebraic group of dimension ≤ d². (2) For a symplectic one of rank 2d, Aut^GSp(D) is a Q_p-algebraic group of dimension ≤ d(2d + 1) + 1.
items.note: The proof's injectivity of Q_p^nr ⊗ End(D) → End(D) must also use ϕ (E2).

items.name: Self-conjugate places
items.statement: Finite places v, v′ of K are conjugate if their restrictions to every CM subfield E of K are exchanged by complex conjugation; v is self-conjugate if conjugate to itself. If K has no CM subfield every finite place is self-conjugate; otherwise v is self-conjugate iff its restriction to the maximal CM subfield is conjugation-invariant; the friendly places of [LV20] are the self-conjugate places unramified over Q (Remark 2.18).
items.note: Generalises LV.1's friendly places.

items.name: Proposition 2.19: Hodge–Tate weights of pure characters
items.statement: Let χ: G_K → Q̄_p^× be unramified and pure of weight n outside a finite set and de Rham at all p-adic places, and let r_v be its Hodge–Tate weight at v | p. If v and v′ are conjugate, r_v + r_{v′} = n; in particular for self-conjugate v, n is even and r_v = n/2.
items.note: Proof via class field theory and the Serre torus [Ser89, II-34]: N_{K/Q}: S_K → G_m is an isogeny when K has no CM subfield, and N_{K/E}, N_{E^+/Q} otherwise. Hodge–Tate weight convention: r with (C_p(r) ⊗ V)^{G_v} ≠ 0.

items.name: Remark 2.20: pure characters at self-conjugate places
items.statement: Under Proposition 2.19's hypotheses, if v is self-conjugate then χ|G_v = χ_0·χ_cyc^{−n/2} with χ_0 of finite order.

items.name: Corollary 2.21: average Hodge–Tate weight
items.statement: Let L/K be finite, V a G_L-representation de Rham above p and unramified and pure of weight n outside finitely many places, and v a self-conjugate place of K above p. Then Σ_{w|v} [L_w : K_v] Σ_i i·dim_{L_w} gr^i_F D_dR,w(V) = n·[L : K]·dim V / 2.
items.note: Proof: apply Proposition 2.19 to det Ind_{G_L}^{G_K} V.

items.name: Parallel transport on rigid neighbourhoods
items.statement: If (E, ∇) is a vector bundle with flat connection on Y^an and U_{y_0} ∋ y_0 is admissible open with H^0_dR(U_{y_0}) = K_v over which (E, ∇) ≃ (O, d)^m, there is a unique T^∇_{y_0}: (O ⊗ E_{y_0}, d) ≅ (E, ∇)|U_{y_0} that is the identity at y_0; its fibres give parallel transport T^∇_{y_0,y}. Such neighbourhoods always exist [Shi20, Theorem 9.7].
items.note: LV.3 plans transport on residue disks of a good model; this is the model-free version.

items.name: The v-adic period map
items.statement: For a filtered vector bundle with flat connection on Y^an (filtration not necessarily Griffiths transverse) and U_{y_0} as above, the period map Φ_{y_0}: U_{y_0} → G^an_{y_0} to the flag variety of filtrations on E_{y_0} classifies the pullback of F^• along T^∇_{y_0}: Φ_{y_0}(y) is the filtration on E_{y_0} pulled back from E_y by T^∇_{y_0,y}.

items.name: Proposition 3.2: the analytified flag variety
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional K_v-space V and dimension data (d_i), the rigid analytification G^an of the flag variety represents S ↦ {exhaustive separated filtrations on O_S ⊗ V with each gr^i a vector bundle of rank d_i}.
items.note: Analytification itself is AdicSpacesPartII R1's.

items.name: Relative de Rham cohomology and Gauss–Manin
items.statement: For π: X → Y smooth proper of smooth K_v-varieties, H^i_dR(X/Y) is a vector bundle with Hodge filtration and flat Gauß–Manin connection [KO68], with fibres H^i_dR(X_y/K_v) by base change.
items.note: A4 plans relative H¹_dR with Gauss–Manin for abelian schemes, which is the case the paper applies.

items.name: Theorem 3.3: period maps control D_pst
items.statement: Let π: X → Y be smooth proper of smooth K_v-varieties and U ⊆ Y^an a closed polydisc over which H^i_dR(X/Y)^an has a full basis of horizontal sections. For y_0, y ∈ U(K_v) there is a unique isomorphism of (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules T_{y_0,y}: D_pst(H^i_ét(X_{y_0,K̄_v})) ≅ D_pst(H^i_ét(X_{y,K̄_v})) compatible, through c_dR ∘ c_BO, with 1 ⊗ T^∇_{y_0,y} on K̄_v ⊗ H^i_dR.
items.locator: arXiv v1 Theorem 3.3, pp.16–17, proved in §3.5
items.note: Unlike LV.4, no good reduction is assumed; the proof uses Scholze's relative comparison and Shimizu's theory.

items.name: Proposition 3.5: period maps and local Galois representations
items.statement: With M^i(Φ) := (H^i_pst(X_{y_0}/Q_p^nr), H^i_dR(X_{y_0}/K_v), c_dR ∘ c_BO) filtered by Φ, for every y ∈ U_{y_0}(K_v) H^i_pH(X_y/K_v) ≃ M^i(Φ_{y_0}(y)) as filtered discrete (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules; since D_pH is fully faithful, Φ_{y_0}(y) determines the isomorphism class of H^i_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p).

items.name: The pro-étale site and its period sheaves
items.statement: For a smooth K_v-analytic space U, the pro-étale site U_proét [Sch13, Def. 3.9; Sch16] carries O_U, Ẑ_{p,U}, B^+_dR,U and the structural de Rham sheaf OB_dR,U, a filtered O_U-algebra with a flat Griffiths-transverse connection extending d, with B^+_dR,U = (F⁰OB_dR,U)^{∇=0}.

items.name: Local systems, filtered bundles and OB_dR-bundles (Definition 3.6)
items.statement: Loc(U, Ẑ_p) (Ẑ_p-local systems), Loc(U, B^+_dR), FMIC(U, O_U) (filtered vector bundles with flat Griffiths-transverse connection) and FMIC(U, OB_dR) (filtered OB_dR-vector bundles with flat connection), with the base-change ⊗-functors (3.1) Loc(U, Ẑ_p) → Loc(U, B^+_dR) → FMIC(U, OB_dR) ← FMIC(U, O_U).

items.name: Proposition 3.7: full faithfulness
items.statement: Loc(U, B^+_dR) → FMIC(U, OB_dR) and FMIC(U, O_U) → FMIC(U, OB_dR) are fully faithful, and the essential image of the second lies in that of the first.
items.note: Extracted from the proof of [Sch13, Theorem 7.6]; Remark 3.8 compares with Scholze's OB^+_dR formulation.

items.name: De Rham pairs
items.statement: A de Rham pair on U is (𝔼, E, c) with 𝔼 a Ẑ_p-local system, E ∈ FMIC(U, O_U) and c: OB_dR ⊗ 𝔼 ≅ OB_dR ⊗ E an isomorphism in FMIC(U, OB_dR) (𝔼 and E are associated [Sch13, Def. 7.5]); they form a ⊗-category, and 𝔼 is de Rham if it is the first component of one. Pullback along f: V → U preserves de Rham pairs (Proposition 3.11).
items.locator: arXiv v1 Definition 3.9, Remark 3.10, Proposition 3.11, p.20

items.name: Derived pushforward of de Rham pairs
items.statement: For π: V → U smooth proper: R^iπ_*𝔼 is a Ẑ_p-local system ([DLLZ19, Cor. 6.3.5], [Sch13, Prop. 8.2]); R^iπ_dR* E := R^iπ_* DR_{V/U}(E) is a filtered O_U-module with Gauß–Manin connection defined by the extension 0 → π^{-1}Ω¹_U ⊗ DR_{V/U}(E)[−1] → DR_V(E)/σ² → DR_{V/U}(E) → 0 (cf. [Kat70, (3.2.4)]); likewise for OB_dR-bundles, with comparison maps η_𝔼 and η_E compatible with connection and filtration.

items.name: Theorem 3.12: Scholze's relative comparison
items.statement: For π: V → U smooth proper of smooth rigid spaces over K_v and a de Rham pair (𝔼, E, c) on V: (1) R^iπ_dR* E is a filtered vector bundle with flat connection; (2) η_𝔼 and η_E become isomorphisms after completing for the filtration; (3) there is a unique c̃: OB_dR ⊗ R^iπ_*𝔼 ≅ OB_dR ⊗ R^iπ_dR* E compatible with R^iπ_dR*(c) after completion. So R^iπ_*(𝔼, E, c) is a de Rham pair.
items.note: [Sch13, Theorems 1.10 and 8.8]; P8 plans the proper-smooth comparison with connection. Remark 3.13: whether η are isomorphisms before completing is left open.

items.name: Lemma 3.14: completion is harmless
items.statement: If M_0, M_1 ∈ FMIC(U, OB_dR) lie in the essential image of Loc(U, B^+_dR), every filtered OB^∧_dR-linear map M_0^∧ → M_1^∧ compatible with connections is the completion of a unique morphism M_0 → M_1, which is an isomorphism iff its completion is.
items.note: Remark 3.15 sketches why B^+_dR,U is complete for its filtration, via [Sch13, Lemmas 3.18, 4.10(v)].

items.name: Proposition 3.16: cup products
items.statement: For π smooth proper and a pairing of de Rham pairs (𝔼_1, E_1, c_1) ⊗ (𝔼_2, E_2, c_2) → (𝔼_3, E_3, c_3) whose pushforwards are local systems, the cup products on R^iπ_* and R^iπ_dR* form a pairing of de Rham pairs R^iπ_*(…) ⊗ R^jπ_*(…) → R^{i+j}π_*(…).

items.name: Proposition 3.17: base change
items.statement: For a commuting square (3.4) with π, π′ smooth proper and a de Rham pair on V whose pushforwards are local systems, R^iπ_dR* E and R^iπ′_dR* g*E are filtered vector bundles with flat connection and the base-change maps (3.5) form a morphism of de Rham pairs f*R^iπ_*(𝔼, E, c) → R^iπ′_* g*(𝔼, E, c).

items.name: Proposition 3.18: algebraic versus analytic pushforwards
items.statement: For π: X → Y smooth proper of smooth K_v-varieties: (1) for E ∈ FMIC(X), R^iπ_dR*(E)^an → R^iπ^an_dR*(E^an) is an isomorphism; (2) for a Z_p-local system 𝔼, R^iπ^an_*(𝔼̂^an) is a Ẑ_p-local system and R^iπ_ét*(𝔼)^{∧,an} → R^iπ^an_*(𝔼̂^an) is an isomorphism [Sch13, Thms 9.1, 9.3, Cor. 3.17, Prop. 8.2].

items.name: The comparison isomorphism c_dR
items.statement: For smooth proper X/L_w, applying Theorem 3.12 to X^an → Sp(L_w) and the unit pair and taking sections over lim Sp(L′_w) gives c_dR: B_dR ⊗ H^i_ét(X_{L̄_w}, Q_p) ≅ B_dR ⊗ H^i_dR(X/L_w) (3.8), B_dR-linear, G_w-equivariant and strictly compatible with filtrations. This (Scholze's) c_dR is the one used throughout (Remark 3.4).
items.note: Remark 3.4: Nizioł's comparison of comparison maps [Niz20] does not cover Scholze's.

items.name: Proposition 3.19: formal compatibilities of c_dR
items.statement: (1) c_dR on H^• is an isomorphism of graded algebras; (2) it is natural in X; (3) it commutes with base change along finite L_{w_2}/L_{w_1}; (4) it respects Künneth isomorphisms.

items.name: Proposition 3.20: duality, cycle and Chern classes
items.statement: There is a G_v-equivariant filtered isomorphism a: B_dR(−1) ≅ B_dR⟨−1⟩ such that: (5) c_dR matches the étale and de Rham trace maps on H^{2n} via a^{⊗n}; (6) it matches the Poincaré duality pairings; (7) c_dR ⊗ a^{⊗−r} identifies étale and de Rham cycle classes of codimension-r cycles (3.10); (8) it identifies étale and de Rham Chern classes of vector bundles.
items.note: The proof of (8) as printed applies (2) and (7) to the non-proper total space of a line bundle (E3). Remark 3.21: a is probably the canonical choice, not proved.

items.name: Theorem 3.22: horizontal de Rham local systems
items.statement: Let U be a closed polydisc or spherical polyannulus over K_v and (𝔼, E, c) a de Rham pair on U with E having a full basis of horizontal sections. For y_0, y ∈ U(K_v) there is a unique isomorphism of (ϕ, N, G_v)-modules T_{y_0,y}: D_pst(𝔼_{ȳ_0}) ≅ D_pst(𝔼_ȳ) compatible, through c_BO and the fibre comparisons c_{y_0}, c_y, with 1 ⊗ T^∇_{y_0,y}.
items.locator: arXiv v1 Theorem 3.22, pp.28–29, proof pp.31–32
items.note: Theorem 3.3 is the special case of the de Rham pair (R^iπ^an_* Ẑ_p, R^iπ^an_dR* O, c_dR). Also in [Bet22, Theorem 6.1].

items.name: Lemma 3.23: reduction to spherical polyannuli
items.statement: If Theorem 3.22 holds for spherical polyannuli over all finite K_v/Q_p, it holds for closed polydiscs: embed a polyannulus through y_0 and y when the residue field is not F_2; otherwise use the unramified extensions of degrees 2 and 3, whose Galois groups generate G_v.

items.name: Shimizu's horizontal semistable periods
items.statement: For R_v = O_v⟨t_1^{±1},…,t_n^{±1}⟩ and G_{R_v} = Aut(R̄_v[p^{-1}]/R_v[p^{-1}]) (a profinite group mapping onto G_v), Shimizu's ring B^∇_st(R_v) with ϕ, N and G_{R_v}-action has (B^∇_st)^{G_{R_w}} = L_{w,0} [Shi20, Cor. 4.10]; D^∇_pst(E) := lim_w (B^∇_st ⊗ E)^{G_{R_w}} is a discrete (ϕ, N, G_v)-module of dimension ≤ rank E, and E is potentially horizontal semistable when equality holds [Shi20, Def. 4.15].

items.name: Lemma 3.25 and Corollary 3.26
items.statement: If E is potentially horizontal semistable, then for a K_v-point y with lift ỹ*, E_ỹ is potentially semistable and ρ_ỹ: D^∇_pst(E) → D_pst(E_ỹ) is an isomorphism [Shi20, Lemma 4.4]; hence T_{y_0,y} := ρ_ỹ ∘ ρ_{ỹ_0}^{-1} is a canonical isomorphism D_pst(E_{ỹ_0}) ≅ D_pst(E_ỹ).

items.name: Lemma 3.27: local systems as G_{R_v}-representations
items.statement: Finite étale coverings of U = Sp(R_v[p^{-1}]) form a Galois category with fibre functor Hom_U(Ũ, −), so Ẑ_p-local systems on U are equivalent to continuous G_{R_v}-representations on finitely generated Z_p-modules, E ↦ H^0(Ũ, E); a lift ỹ of a K_v-point identifies H^0(Ũ, E)_ỹ ≅ E_ȳ (Remark 3.28), and G_{R_v} is de Jong's algebraic fundamental group (Remark 3.29).

items.name: Abelian-by-finite families
items.statement: An abelian-by-finite family X → Y′ → Y over a scheme Y is a surjective finite étale Y′ → Y and a polarised abelian scheme X → Y′ (polarisation λ) [LV20, Definition 5.1].

items.name: Étale cohomology of a fibre and the polarisation pairing
items.statement: Over a field K of characteristic 0: H^k_ét ≅ ∧^k_{H^0_ét} H^1_ét, and H^•_ét = ∏_{y′} Ind ∧^• H^1_ét(X_{ȳ′}) (4.1). c^ét_1(λ) := ½ c^ét_1((1, λ)*P) ∈ H^2_ét(1)^{G_K} gives an H^0-linear G_K-equivariant pairing ω̌^ét_λ on H^ét_1 := Hom_{H^0}(H^1, H^0).

items.name: Lemma 4.2
items.statement: ω̌^ét_λ: ∧²_{H^0} H^ét_1 → H^0_ét(1) is perfect, i.e. H^ét_1 ≅ H^1_ét(1). Hence ω^ét_λ: ∧²_{H^0} H^1_ét → H^0_ét(−1) is a perfect pairing and (H^1_ét, H^0_ét(−1), ω^ét_λ) is a symplectic H^0_ét-module.
items.note: Via the Weil pairing on the Tate module up to sign ([OSZ21, Lemma 2.6]).

items.name: Symplectic modules and symplectic pairs
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Q_p-algebra A with continuous G_K-action, a symplectic A-module is (V, L, ω) with V finite locally free, L free of rank 1 and ω: ∧²_A V → L a perfect G_K-equivariant A-linear pairing (Definition 4.3). A symplectic pair is (A, V); these form a category SP(Rep_{Q_p}(G_K)) (Definition 4.4), and similarly in other ⊗-categories. Example 4.5: H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p) := (H^0_ét, H^1_ét) for y ∈ Y(K).

items.name: De Rham side: Lemma 4.6
items.statement: H^•_dR ≅ ∧^•_{H^0_dR} H^1_dR ≅ ∏_{y′} ∧^• H^1_dR(X_{y′}/K(y′)) (4.2); c^dR_1(λ) ∈ F¹H²_dR gives ω̌^dR_λ: ∧²_{H^0_dR} H^dR_1 → H^0_dR⟨1⟩, which is perfect (by comparison with Lemma 4.2), so (H^1_dR, H^0_dR⟨−1⟩, ω^dR_λ) is a symplectic H^0_dR-module in filtered vector spaces and F¹H¹_dR is a Lagrangian H^0_dR-submodule.

items.name: The symplectic pair of p-adic Hodge cohomology
items.statement: Over K_v, c_dR (Propositions 3.19–3.20) identifies c^ét_1(λ) with c^dR_1(λ), so ω̌^ét_λ and ω̌^dR_λ correspond, and H^{≤1}_pH(X_y/K_v) := (H^0_pH, H^1_pH) is a symplectic pair in MF(ϕ, N, G_v) with pairing ω^pH_λ.

items.name: Lemma 4.7: relative de Rham Chern classes
items.statement: For π: X → Y smooth of smooth varieties over a field of characteristic 0 and a line bundle L on X there is c^dR_1(L)/Y ∈ F¹H^0(Y, H²_dR(X/Y))^{∇=0} whose fibre at every y ∈ Y(L) is c^dR_1(L|X_y).
items.note: Built from dlog: O_X^× → Ω^•_{X/K}[1] and the Leray spectral sequence [Har75, §7.7].

items.name: Lemma 4.8 and Remark 4.9
items.statement: The relative pairing ω^dR_λ: ∧² H^1_dR → H^0_dR⟨−1⟩ on Y is perfect. On a closed polydisc U_{y_0} over which H^0_dR and H^1_dR have full bases of flat sections, parallel transport for i = 0, 1 respects the algebra, module and pairing structures; in particular Y′ → Y becomes trivial over U_{y_0}, (Y′)^an|U_{y_0} ≅ U_{y_0} × (Y′_{y_0})^an.

items.name: The Lagrangian period domain
items.statement: H_{y_0} ⊆ G_{y_0} is the K_v-variety of Lagrangian H^0_dR(X_{y_0}/K_v)-submodules of H^1_dR(X_{y_0}/K_v); by Lemma 4.8 the period map of an abelian-by-finite family lands in H^an_{y_0}.

items.name: The symplectic pairs M^{≤1}(Φ)
items.statement: For Φ ∈ H_{y_0}(K_v), M^1(Φ) := (H^1_pst(X_{y_0}/Q_p^nr), H^1_dR(X_{y_0}/K_v), c_dR ∘ c_BO) with F^i = H^1_dR (i ≤ 0), Φ (i = 1), 0 (i ≥ 2); it is a symplectic module over M^0 := (H^0_pst, H^0_dR, c_dR ∘ c_BO), and M^{≤1}(Φ) := (M^0, M^1(Φ)).

items.name: Proposition 4.11
items.statement: For an abelian-by-finite family over a smooth K_v-variety Y, y_0 ∈ Y(K_v) and a closed polydisc U_{y_0} over which H^0_dR and H^1_dR have full bases of horizontal sections, D_pH(H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄_v}, Q_p)) ≃ M^{≤1}(Φ_{y_0}(y)) as symplectic pairs in MF(ϕ, N, G_v) for every y ∈ U_{y_0}(K_v) (diagram of §4.2).

items.name: Decomposition of the period domain (Lemma 4.12)
items.statement: With the closed points y′_i of Y′_{y_0} and L_{w_i} := K_v(y′_i), H_{y_0} = ∏_i Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i}, H_{y′_i} := LGrass(H^1_dR(X_{y′_i}/L_{w_i})) (4.3), and for Φ = ∏ Φ′_i, M^1(Φ) = ∏_i Ind^{G_v}_{G_{w_i}} M^1_i(Φ′_i) compatibly with symplectic structures over M^0 ≅ ∏_i Ind^{G_v}_{G_{w_i}} 1.
items.note: Corrected statement: the lemma prints H^1_dR(X_{y′_0}/L_{w_i}) for X_{y′_i} (E4).

items.name: Complex period maps
items.statement: For Y smooth connected over C, a simply connected étale neighbourhood U_{y_0} of y_0 and a filtered flat bundle E, the complex period map Φ_{ỹ_0}: U_{y_0} → G^an_{y_0} classifies the pullback of F^• along the Riemann–Hilbert trivialisation T^∇_{ỹ_0}.

items.name: Lemma 5.1
items.statement: The Zariski closure of the image of the complex period map does not depend on the simply connected étale neighbourhood U_{y_0}.

items.name: Lemma 5.2
items.statement: The Zariski closure of the image of Φ_{ỹ_0} contains the monodromy orbit π_1(Y^an, y_0)·h_0 of the point h_0 given by F^•E_{y_0}; on the universal cover the orbit lies in the image itself.
items.note: LV Lemma 3.1, which LV.3 plans.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: v-adic and complex Zariski closures agree
items.statement: Let Y be smooth geometrically connected over K_v, y_0 ∈ Y(K_v), (E, ∇, F^•) an algebraic filtered flat bundle, and ι: K_v ↪ C. The Zariski closure Z_v ⊆ G_{y_0} of the image of the v-adic period map and the closure Z_∞ ⊆ G_{y_0,C} of the image of the complex period map satisfy Z_∞ = Z_{v,C}.
items.note: [LV20, §3.4] does this for y_0 ∈ Y(K); here y_0 need only be K_v-rational.

items.name: Lemmas 5.4–5.6 and Remark 5.7: the formal germ
items.statement: The Zariski closure of the v-adic image does not depend on the neighbourhood (Lemma 5.4). With a trivialisation E = O^m and the unique T ∈ GL_m(K_v[[t]]) with dT = −ωT, T|_{t=0} = I (5.1) [Kat70, Prop. 8.9], both period maps are given by T_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ T_{m_i}, so Z_v and Z_∞ are the scheme-theoretic images of Φ̂_{y_0} over K_v and C (Lemmas 5.5, 5.6); Φ̂_{y_0} is intrinsic and defined over any subfield over which the data are (Remark 5.7).

items.name: Full monodromy
items.statement: X → Y′ → Y over a smooth connected complex Y has full monodromy if the Zariski closure of the monodromy image in GL(H^1_B(X_{y_0}, Q)) contains ∏_{y′_0} Sp(H^1_B(X_{y′_0}, Q)); over a field of characteristic 0 this is defined through a complex embedding ι.

items.name: Lemma 5.9
items.statement: If Y is smooth geometrically connected over K_v and X → Y′ → Y has full monodromy for some ι: K_v ↪ C, then for every y_0 ∈ Y(K_v) the v-adic period map Φ_{y_0}: U_{y_0} → H^an_{y_0} has Zariski-dense image.

items.name: Corollary 5.10 and Remark 5.11
items.statement: If Y is a smooth curve over K_v, X → Y′ → Y has full monodromy and U_{y_0} is a closed disc as above, then any C_0 ⊆ U_{y_0}(K_v) with Φ_{y_0}(C_0) not Zariski-dense in H_{y_0} is finite; by compactness a subset C ⊆ Y(K_v) whose images are non-dense for all y_0 is finite.

items.name: The adelic Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
items.statement: Y(A_K)^LV_X ⊆ Y(A_K) is the set of (y_u) for which some symplectic pair (A, V) of G_K-representations satisfies H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_u,K̄_u}, Q_p) ≅ (A|G_u, V|G_u) for every place u (it interpolates the y_u); Y(K_v)^LV_X is its projection.

items.name: S-good pairs and the Lawrence–Venkatesh locus
items.statement: (A, V) is S-good if A is unramified outside S; V is unramified, pure and integral of weight 1 outside S; and V is de Rham above p with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1}. For suitable S (containing the places above p∞ and of bad reduction), Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is the set of y_v ∈ Y(K_v) with H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) ≅ (A|G_v, V|G_v) for some S-good (A, V). Requiring A to be an Artin representation changes nothing (Remark 6.3).
items.locator: arXiv v1 Definitions 1.2 and 6.2, Remark 6.3, pp.2, 43–44

items.name: The Lawrence–Venkatesh locus in the period domain
items.statement: H_{y_0}(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is the set of Φ ∈ H_{y_0}(K_v) with M^0 ≅ D_pH(A|G_v) and M^1(Φ) ≅ D_pH(V|G_v) for some S-good (A, V). Φ_{y_0} maps U_{y_0}(K_v) ∩ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} into it, so Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is finite once (i) every Φ_{y_0} has Zariski-dense image and (ii) H_{y_0}(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is not Zariski-dense.

items.name: Lemma 6.4
items.statement: If S contains the places above p∞ and of bad reduction and (A, V) interpolates y ∈ Y(A_K)^LV_X, then (A, V) is S-good; hence Y(K_v)^LV_X ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S}.

items.name: Theorem 6.5
items.statement: If v is self-conjugate, there is an abelian-by-finite family X → Y′ → Y for which Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} is finite for all suitable S.
items.locator: arXiv v1 Theorem 6.5, p.44, proof §6.5, p.53
items.note: Take the Kodaira–Parshin family with q as in Proposition 6.20.

items.name: Mordell from Theorem 6.5
items.statement: Y(K) ⊆ Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} for every abelian-by-finite family (interpolate by H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y,K̄}, Q_p), S-good by Lemma 6.4), so Theorem 6.5 reproves the Mordell conjecture.

items.name: Remark 6.6: the algebra of a fibre
items.statement: H^0_ét(X_{y_v,K̄_v}, Q_p) = ∏_{Y′_{y_v}(K̄_v)} Q_p, so Q̄_p-algebra maps ψ from it are the K̄_v-points of Y′_{y_v}, i.e. a closed point y′_v with a K_v-embedding of K_v(y′_v); [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 means [K_v(y′_v) : K_v] ≥ 4.

items.name: Proposition 6.7: the principal trichotomy (corrected)
items.statement: Let v be self-conjugate and (A, V) a symplectic pair of G_K-representations, V of rank 2d > 0 over A, de Rham above p with Hodge–Tate weights in {0, 1} at v, unramified and pure of weight 1 outside a finite set; Σ = Σ_A the Q̄_p-points of A. Then (a) some ψ ∈ Σ has [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 and V_ψ GSp-irreducible for G_ψ; or (b) some ψ with [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4 has a non-zero isotropic G_ψ-stable W ≤ V_ψ with dim F¹D_dR,w_ψ(W) ≥ ½ dim W; or (c) the number of ψ ∈ Σ with [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] < 4 is ≥ #Σ/(d + 1), which is ≥ dim_{Q_p}(A)/(d + 1) when A is étale.
items.locator: arXiv v1 Proposition 6.7, pp.46–47; Proposition 1.8, pp.5–6; Remark 1.9, p.6
items.note: Corrected statement: as printed, (c) has dim_{Q_p}(A), which fails for non-reduced A (E1). Every use has A étale. Proposition 1.8 states (b) with a local G_{w_ψ}-subrepresentation, a weaker conclusion.

items.name: Types (a), (b), (c) and their loci
items.statement: Type (a): an S-good (A, V) with some ψ, [G_v : G_{w_ψ}] ≥ 4, V_ψ GSp-irreducible; type (b): a pair of G_v-representations with some ψ, index ≥ 4, and a non-zero isotropic G_{w_ψ}-subrepresentation of average Hodge–Tate weight ≥ 1/2; type (c): an algebra A with #{ψ : index < 4} ≥ dim(A)/(d + 1). Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)}, Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)}, Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(c)} are the corresponding loci, and for self-conjugate v, Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S} lies in their union.

items.name: Proposition 6.9
items.statement: For y_0 ∈ Y(K_v), the set H_{y_0}(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} of Φ with M^{≤1}(Φ) ≅ (D_pH(A|G_v), D_pH(V|G_v)) for an S-good pair of type (a) is not Zariski-dense in H_{y_0}.

items.name: Corollary 6.10
items.statement: If X → Y′ → Y has full monodromy, Y(K_v)^LV_{X,S,(a)} is finite.

items.name: The sets T_i and their finiteness (Lemma 6.12)
items.statement: T_i is the set of isomorphism classes of symplectic 1-modules D of rank 2d_i in MF(ϕ, N, G_{w_i}) for which there are L/K of degree ≤ δ := deg(Y′ → Y) unramified outside S, a v-adic place w_i of L with L_{w_i} ≅ K_v(y′_i), and a GSp-irreducible symplectic G_L-representation V, de Rham above p and unramified, pure and integral of weight 1 outside S, with D ≅ D_pH,w_i(V|G_{w_i}). Each T_i is finite (Hermite–Minkowski and Lemma 2.4).

items.name: Lemma 6.13
items.statement: If [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4, the set H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(a) of Lagrangians Φ′_i with M^1_i(Φ′_i) ∈ T_i is not Zariski-dense in Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i} (though it may be dense in H_{y′_i}, Remark 6.14).
items.note: Checked by cc-442dc5: [L_{w_i} : K_v]·d_i(d_i + 1)/2 ≥ 2d_i² + 2d_i > d_i(2d_i + 1).

items.name: Proposition 6.15
items.statement: The set H_{y_0}(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} of Φ with M^{≤1}(Φ) ≅ (D_pH(A), D_pH(V)) for a symplectic pair of de Rham G_v-representations of type (b) is not Zariski-dense in H_{y_0}.
items.note: Corrected statement: the text writes M^1(Φ) for the pair M^{≤1}(Φ) (E5).

items.name: Corollary 6.16
items.statement: If X → Y′ → Y has full monodromy, Y(K_v)^LV_{X,(b)} is finite.

items.name: Lemma 6.17
items.statement: If [L_{w_i} : K_v] ≥ 4, the set H_{y′_i}(L_{w_i})_(b) of Lagrangians Φ′_i for which M^1_i(Φ′_i) has a non-zero isotropic filtered (ϕ, N, G_{w_i})-submodule D with dim F¹D_dR ≥ ½ dim D_pst is not Zariski-dense in Res^{L_{w_i}}_{K_v} H_{y′_i}.
items.note: Via (6.1), K̄_v ⊗ Res H_{y′_i} ≅ LGrass(K̄_v ⊗ H^1_pst)^r with the r factors related by σ_j ⊗ ϕ^{m_j}, and Sublemma 6.18. Generalises LV Lemma 6.3 from φ-modules.

items.name: Sublemma 6.18
items.statement: Let (V, ω) be a symplectic space over a field F and r ≥ 4. The r-tuples of Lagrangians (Φ_s) for which some non-zero isotropic W ≤ V has dim(Φ_j ∩ W) ≥ ½ dim W for all j lie in a proper Zariski-closed subset of LGrass(V, ω)^r.
items.note: Checked by cc-442dc5: the four Lagrangians Φ_1, Φ_2 and the graphs of ψ_3(e_α) = f_α and ψ_4(e_α) = λ_αf_α (distinct λ_α) admit no such W. [LV20, Lemma 6.4] needs r ≥ 5 but no isotropy.

items.name: The Kodaira–Parshin family (cited)
items.statement: For an odd prime q, [LV20, §7] constructs an abelian-by-finite family X_q → Y′_q → Y of constant relative dimension d_q = (g − 1/2)(q − 1) with full monodromy [LV20, §8.2.3], and Y′_{q,y}(K̄_v) ≅ Surj^{out,*}(π_1^ét(Y_K̄_v − y), Aff(q)) G_v-equivariantly (surjections non-trivial on an inertia generator at y, up to conjugation).
items.note: Footnote 23: [LV20, Lemma 2.11] is stated without the quotient by conjugation, which acts freely since Aff(q) has trivial centre.

items.name: Proposition 6.20
items.statement: If q − 1 is divisible neither by 4 nor by any odd prime divisor of q_v(q_v + 1)(q_v³ − 1), and q − 1 ≥ 9n_v with n_v the number of extensions of K_v of degree 2 or 3 in K̄_v, then Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,(c)} = ∅.
items.note: Checked by cc-442dc5: G_v-fixed subgroups of M = H^1_ét(Y_K̄_v, Z/k), k = (q − 1)/2, for G_w of index 2 or 3 are isotropic for the Weil pairing since gcd(k, q_v^i − 1) = 1, i ≤ 3, and the chain ζ(2g)n_v/k^g < 9n_v/(8k^g) ≤ 1/(4k^{g−1}) < 1/(d_q + 1) holds.

items.name: Remark 6.21
items.statement: n_v is bounded in terms of K; if v ∤ 6 then n_v = 7 (three quadratic and four cubic extensions of K_v in K̄_v).

items.name: Corollary 6.22
items.statement: For every finite place v of K there is an abelian-by-finite family of constant positive relative dimension with full monodromy and Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,(c)} = ∅ (a Kodaira–Parshin family, q chosen by Dirichlet's theorem).

items.name: Dirichlet's theorem
items.statement: For a positive integer m and a unit a mod m, and every n, there is a prime q > n with q ≡ a mod m.
items.locator: arXiv v1 used in Corollary 6.22, p.53
items.note: Read at Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/PrimesInAP.lean:442.

items.name: Remark 6.23: which (v, q) work
items.statement: The paper's proof gives finiteness of Y(K_v)^LV_{X_q,S} when (1) v is self-conjugate; (2) q − 1 is prime to 4 and to the odd primes dividing q_v ∏_{i≤3}(q_v^i − 1); (3) n_v ζ(2g) 2^g/(q − 1)^g < 1/((g − 1/2)(q − 1) + 1), with n_v replaceable by 2 at good reduction. [LV20] needs friendly v ∤ 2, i ≤ 7 in (2), 4 in place of n_v, and a good model (1°–4°). (I) For K without CM subfield, 1°–4° hold at 100% of places for suitable q; (II) they fail at ramified places, places above 2 and bad places; (III) for genus 3 the least q is 23 for 1°–4° and 11 for (1)–(3).
items.note: Checked by cc-442dc5: the values 23 and 11 in (III). For (I), see E6.

items.name: The relative symplectic pair R^{≤1}π_ét*Q_p
items.statement: For π: X → Y an abelian-by-finite family, ∧^•_{π_*Q_p} R¹π_ét*Q_p ≅ R^•π_ét*Q_p; the relative Chern class c^ét_1(λ)/Y ∈ H^0(Y, R²π_ét*Q_p(1)), built from the Kummer sequence and the Leray spectral sequence, gives a perfect pairing ω_λ: ∧² R¹π_ét*Q_p → π_ét*Q_p(−1), so (π_ét*Q_p, R¹π_ét*Q_p) is a symplectic pair of Q_p-local systems whose fibres are H^{≤1}_ét(X_ȳ, Q_p).

items.name: Representations attached to a section
items.statement: With A, V the π_1^ét(Y, η̄)-representations of π_ét*Q_p and R¹π_ét*Q_p, a section s gives the symplectic pair (A_s, V_s) of G_K-representations by restriction along s; its isomorphism class depends only on the conjugacy class of s and not on the base point η̄.

items.name: Proposition 7.2
items.statement: If s|G_u is the section of y_u ∈ Y(K_u), then (A_s|G_u, V_s|G_u) ≅ H^{≤1}_ét(X_{y_u,K̄_u}, Q_p) as symplectic pairs of G_u-representations.

items.name: Theorem 7.1
items.statement: For every abelian-by-finite family X → Y′ → Y, the image of loc_v: Sec^Sel(Y/K) → Y(K_v) lies in Y(K_v)^LV_X; indeed (A_s, V_s) interpolates the adelic point of a Selmer section s.

items.name: Filtered derived categories
items.statement: SKom(A) is the category of decreasing sequences of complexes; filtered quasi-isomorphisms are termwise, graded quasi-isomorphisms are those on gr^i := cone(F^{i+1} → F^i); FD(A) localises at the filtered ones (as in [SS16], [BMS19]), while [Sch13] and [GP18] localise at the graded ones (Remark A.4). Cohomology objects H^j(A) are sequences, filtered only in good cases (§A.1). For the large pro-étale site one works with κ-small sheaves (Remark A.5).
items.locator: arXiv v1 Appendix A, Remarks A.1, A.4, A.5, pp.56–58

items.name: Lemma A.2 (Deligne)
items.statement: If A is a filtered complex with filtration bounded below in each degree and its spectral sequence degenerates at the first page, then each H^j(A) is filtered [Del71, Prop. 1.3.2].

items.name: Lemma A.3
items.statement: If A → B is a graded quasi-isomorphism in SKom(A) and A has filtered cohomology objects, then (1) so does B, and (2) H^j(A)^∧ → H^j(B)^∧ is an isomorphism for all j.
